**Finding: MISSING (deviation) — WARRANTY**

**What I found**

- **§ 9 "TRUELINK WARRANTIES" (p0059–p0060)** is the only TrueLink warranty in the agreement, and it covers *only* Y2K date processing. There is no workmanlike-performance warranty, no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy.
- **§ 8 (p0050–p0058)** runs entirely the other way — Client compliance with laws, Client IP warranties, and even a Client no-malicious-code warranty (p0056). The asymmetry is stark.
- **p0042** further disclaims any TrueLink warranty as to the truth or completeness of transmitted credit data.
- **p0076** disclaims implied warranties but is prefaced *"EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT,"* so it does **not** swallow an added express warranty — no carve-out redline is needed, which keeps the edit minimal. As drafted, however, the practical effect is close to an AS IS deal (our walk-away position).

**Redline (validated, ok:true)** — single paragraph inserted after p0060, inside the existing § 9, so no renumbering is required: workmanlike performance of Hosting/Support Services; 12-month software and 90-day services conformance; compliance with laws; no malicious code; TrueLink-elected re-performance/repair/replacement/refund; plus a short belt-and-braces line confirming the express warranties are not disclaimed elsewhere.

**Fallback flagged in the comment:** 90 days software / 30 days services with the same remedies, if TrueLink resists the 12-month period.

One judgment call worth surfacing: the agreement has no defined "Documentation" or "Specifications" term (§ 1 defines neither, and even "Interface" is undefined), so the conformance hook I drafted refers to "its documentation and specifications" generically. That is workable but softer than ideal — if you want a harder standard, the cleaner fix would be to attach a specifications exhibit and cross-reference it, which is a larger edit than this rule warrants.
